messages.content:
You are a clinical validator checking whether a PTSD case
vignette accurately reflects a patient's required cognitive connections.

You will receive:
- A vignette to validate
- A list of REQUIRED edges that must appear
- A list of ACTIVE components that must appear

---

COMPONENT SYNONYMS
Each component may appear by its exact name or any accepted synonym:
  Triggers            → "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals → "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory              → "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat              → "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies → "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "maladaptive coping", "safety behaviours"

---

CAUSAL STANDARD
A required edge A→B is SATISFIED if, within the same paragraph:
  - Both A and B (or their synonyms) appear, AND
  - The paragraph conveys — through any language — that A influences, drives, or leads to B.
This includes direct causal sentences, sequential structure, or connecting phrases
like "because of", "this meant", "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
A required edge is MISSING only if no paragraph conveys the A→B relationship at all.

---

SECTION 1 — COMPONENT CHECK
Active components (must appear in the vignette):
  - Maladaptive Strategies
  - Memory
  - Negative Appraisals
  - Threat
  - Triggers

Confirm each component appears as a described feature of the patient's presentation.
This is an internal check only — do NOT add component results to violations.

---

SECTION 2 — REQUIRED EDGES
  - Triggers → Memory
  - Triggers → Negative Appraisals
  - Negative Appraisals → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Negative Appraisals → Threat
  - Negative Appraisals → Triggers
  - Memory → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Memory → Threat
  - Memory → Negative Appraisals
  - Threat → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Threat → Negative Appraisals
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Memory
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Threat

For each edge, apply the causal standard above.
- If satisfied: do nothing — only failures are reported.
- If missing: add it to violations and explain in one sentence what causal relationship is absent.

Validate the following vignette against the cognitive graph.

Bao, a 46-year-old firefighter, moves through the station with a coiled stillness that his crew has learned to treat like a downed power line. It has been three years since his deployment as a relief worker, and the man who returned is not the one who left. The easy camaraderie he once shared with his team has been replaced by a tense perimeter of silence, a space his colleagues are afraid to cross. His ex-wife had called it living with a ghost.

The ghost was born in a village reduced to rubble and dust. Bao was helping to distribute medical supplies when the mortar hit the marketplace. The world dissolved into a deafening bang, a wave of force that threw him against a wall, searing his ribs with a pain that still visits him in his sleep. In the chaos that followed, the veneer of civilization cracked. He saw a man, no older than his own son, looting supplies from an injured woman, and something inside Bao froze. He did nothing. Moments later, from the shelter of a collapsed storefront, he overheard the triumphant, jeering comments of soldiers dragging a young girl away. He could not find the words then, and he cannot find them now, to describe the sounds that followed. The sequence of that day remains a blur of disjointed images and sounds, a confusing loop of failure he cannot put in order.

Back home, the sounds of the city became a minefield. A car backfiring on the street outside the firehouse is enough to trigger a flashback, not as a clear narrative, but as a sensory assault: the smell of dust and cordite, the sharp, phantom pain blooming in his ribs. This sudden recall of physical agony floods him with a raw, nameless horror. The fragmented memory of his inaction—seeing the theft, hearing the soldiers—invariably follows, cementing the appraisal that he acted in ways that go against everything he is. He is no longer a helper, a protector; he is a man who stood by. This belief has become the lens through which he sees everything. When he sees people misbehaving on the news or cutting in line at the store, it doesn’t just irritate him; it’s a personal confirmation of his own moral failure, a trigger that sends him spiraling back into shame.

This crushing self-appraisal dictates his life. The certainty that he has violated his own values leaves him perpetually on edge, his anger a hot wire just beneath his skin. This constant state of threat reinforces his belief that his life has been destroyed by the trauma, that the good man he thought he was is gone forever. To manage the overwhelming guilt and rage, he has developed a series of desperate strategies. He tries to suppress the memories, pushing them down with all his might, but this effort only seems to make them resurface more violently later, more jumbled and terrifying. The failure of this suppression leaves him feeling even more agitated and unsafe.

The conviction that he is a contaminated person, that he no longer belongs anywhere, has driven him to seek control in meticulous, private rituals. Before every shift, he mentally recites the names of every person he has ever saved as a firefighter, a magical attempt to balance the scales and prevent more bad things from happening. But when a memory breaks through, or the feeling of worthlessness becomes unbearable, the rituals are not enough. In those moments of intense threat, he retreats to his car or a bathroom stall and digs his fingernails into his forearms until the physical pain is sharp enough to eclipse the emotional torment. He has come to believe this is a necessary penance.

These cycles have cost him everything. His constant irritability and emotional distance eroded his marriage until it crumbled. At work, he feels like an outsider. The unusual silence of the station between calls feels menacing, pregnant with unspoken danger. He can’t join the casual banter, terrified a stray comment about a news story involving sexual violence will reveal the monster he believes he is. He is convinced he is fundamentally broken, a man whose life was shattered not just by a mortar, but by his own cowardice. Bao finally sought therapy after his captain found him in the locker room, fists clenched and shaking, after a routine fire alarm test. He said he didn’t know if he could be fixed, but he was terrified of what would happen if he didn’t try to find a way to live with the man he had become.

violation_explanations: The vignette does not show how Bao's negative beliefs about himself cause him to perceive more situations as triggers or reminders of the trauma.
